clue.text: City finance needed for company flotation

definitions.meaning: the chief city of a country
a firm floated on the stock market raises money, its funds or stock

explanation.surface: A banker explains what money a firm needs before going public.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a seat of government such as London and the money a business is founded on.

clue.text: Saucy advice to a laggard

definitions.meaning: a variant spelling of the tomato condiment, a sauce
a straggler is urged to close the gap

explanation.surface: A cheeky word of encouragement to someone falling behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old spelling of the tomato condiment and a call to reach those ahead.

clue.text: Urge all delegates to find a means of telling the media

definitions.text: a means of telling the media

parts.note: to press is to urge
a conference is a gathering of delegates

explanation.surface: Delegates are pushed to find a way to brief journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists are invited to a briefing where an announcement is made and questions taken.

clue.text: A drawer of money is required to fork out

definitions.meaning: a cash drawer in a shop counter
to turn over soil with a fork, cultivate

explanation.surface: A cashier is told they must pay up from the drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a shop's cash drawer and also to cultivate land.

clue.text: Evidence that exasperated employer has lost his hair

definitions.text: Evidence that exasperated employer has lost his hair

parts.words: Evidence that exasperated employer has lost his hair
parts.note: a boss who shuts workers out in a dispute is pictured as an angry man pulling a strand of hair from his head

explanation.surface: A frustrated boss has been tearing his hair out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, a strand of hair is gone; really an employer barring staff from work during a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer's exclusion of workers from the workplace during an industrial dispute.

clue.text: A lone walker's cry of derision?

definitions.text: A lone walker's cry of derision?

parts.words: A lone walker's cry of derision
parts.note: Kipling wrote of the cat that walked by himself, so the lone walker is a cat and its cry is a call; a jeering whistle at a performer bears the same name

explanation.surface: A solitary hiker shouts scornfully at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or jeer from an audience expresses scorn for a performer.

clue.text: Wrinkles somewhat smaller than winkles

definitions.meaning: puckers or creases
small edible bivalve shellfish sold alongside winkles

explanation.surface: A comparison of creases with the size of sea snails.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means puckers and also small shellfish sold at British seaside stalls.

clue.text: All in France propose one another'shealth

definitions.meaning: the French word for everyone
a toast to ourselves, read as two English words

explanation.surface: French diners raise a glass to each other's health.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word means everyone, and the same letters split as an English toast to ourselves.

clue.text: Basic beliefs published in religious magazines

definitions.meaning: fundamental tenets of a creed
pieces of writing on belief printed in church periodicals

explanation.surface: Core doctrines appear in print in church publications.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tenets of a creed and, read literally, pieces about belief in a journal.

clue.text: Flatter way to apply plaster

definitions.meaning: to praise excessively
a plasterer spreads it on the wall

explanation.surface: Instructions for spreading plaster smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means pile on praise and literally spread a coat on a surface.

clue.text: Will never get into debt here in the Midlands?

definitions.text: Will never get into debt here in the Midlands?

parts.words: Will never get into debt here in the Midlands
parts.note: an account in credit is said to be in the black, never in the red; the industrial West Midlands region bears that colour in its name

explanation.surface: A remark about thrifty folk from the English Midlands who avoid owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: The industrial area around Birmingham and Wolverhampton in England is named for its soot; the clue pretends the colour means a healthy bank balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The name refers to the old coal-mining and iron-working region west of Birmingham.

clue.text: It is partly covered by a shapely shoe

definitions.text: It is partly covered by a shapely shoe

parts.words: It is partly covered by a shapely shoe
parts.note: stockings on the foot and ankle are partly concealed when a smart shoe is worn

explanation.surface: A remark about an elegant piece of footwear covering something.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings, the legwear in the old hosiery sense, sit inside a shoe and are partly hidden by it.

clue.text: Passes wound round one core

parts.note: each turn of wire wrapped about a central iron former in an electrical device is one pass; the whole winding is described

explanation.surface: Turns of wire are wrapped around a single central rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops of wire wound in a spiral around a former make up the windings of a transformer or electromagnet.

clue.text: Tax which makes a difference to cost

indicators.note: a change made to the letters of the following word rearranges them into a new word

explanation.surface: A levy that alters what something costs.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a levy or payment, surviving in the phrase scot-free, meaning without paying.

clue.text: American state reviews taxes

indicators.note: taking a fresh look reorders the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A US state reassesses its levies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Star State is the second-largest of the United States.

clue.text: Scallops make father sick

parts.note: FR is short for Father, a priest's title
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Eating shellfish has made the priest unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are a wavy ornamental edging, as is a ruffle on a dress.

clue.text: Stick out for a scheme requiring concerted effort

definitions.meaning: to protrude or jut
a planned undertaking needing joint work

explanation.surface: Someone holding firm through a big team plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for jutting forward and a noun for a planned enterprise.

clue.text: Ambition in a boy to become an operator

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another, the desire sitting within the young male

parts.note: a son is a boy
an urge is a strong desire, an ambition

explanation.surface: A lad dreams of growing up to work in the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical specialist who performs operations is said to operate on patients.

clue.text: Don't join in the chorus

definitions.meaning: to abstain or hold back
the repeated lines of a song

explanation.surface: An instruction to a singer to stay silent for the chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning hold back and a noun for the recurring verse of a song.

clue.text: Woke up to the sound of thunder apparently

definitions.meaning: realised the truth about, saw through
thunder makes a low rolling noise

explanation.surface: Someone was woken by a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means found out or saw through, and also made a deep rolling noise.

clue.text: For the fisherman it would mean expenses outstripping takings

definitions.text: For the fisherman it would mean expenses outstripping takings

parts.words: For the fisherman it would mean expenses outstripping takings
parts.note: the accounting term for a deficit is read as a mesh trap going missing at sea

explanation.surface: An angler's business is running at a deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounting term for when costs exceed income over a period.

clue.text: Not yet even two years old, yet a unique specimen

definitions.text: Not yet even two years old
definitions.meaning: a toddler of that age has had just a single birthday
a solitary example, the sole one of its kind

explanation.surface: A rare infant prodigy, the sole example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a child aged a single year and an item with no equal.

clue.text: One who disagrees with the work model

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a poser is one who poses, as a model does

explanation.surface: A sitter for an artwork argues with the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes a motion or idea disagrees with it.

clue.text: Pledge to get the wage estimate reduced?

parts.note: to earn is to get a wage

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its ending, as in a written abbreviation

explanation.surface: A worker promises to accept a smaller pay estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit given as a guarantee of a bargain is a pledge.

clue.text: Sounds like German money is for Karl

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.note: the mark was the currency of Germany before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone notes that Deutschmarks suit the economist Karl.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl is the first name of the philosopher who wrote Das Kapital.

clue.text: Halt and point to a step of mine

parts.note: to halt is to stop
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A miner is told to stop and indicate a step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepped excavation in a mine from which ore is cut is given this mining term.

clue.text: Where one travels in the course of a safari

indicators.note: the letters lie within the word that follows, encountered along the way

explanation.surface: A traveller describes where the trail goes on a safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers go a long way off, to distant places.

clue.text: Investor making a fast buck!

parts.note: a speculator who buys new shares to sell at once for quick profit shares a name with a male deer

explanation.surface: A speculator turning a quick profit on shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A market speculator who applies for new issues to sell immediately, and a male deer.

clue.text: Once written the legal proceedings can begin

definitions.meaning: an archaic past participle of the verb to write
a court order that starts a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A lawyer says the case can start once the papers are drafted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old form meaning penned and also a court summons opening a case.

clue.text: Time employed in complaint about the long-winded parson

definitions.meaning: the years worked for an employer
a congregation grumbling at a vicar would moan about how long his church worship ran

explanation.surface: Worshippers grumble about a vicar who preaches too long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means years in a job and, read literally, how long a church rite lasts.

clue.text: Medico moves gingerly and pulls up from the river

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medico
to edge is to move carefully, bit by bit

explanation.surface: A doctor creeps cautiously and hauls something out of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging scoops silt or objects up from a riverbed.

clue.text: The sort of cog-wheel that makes a chatter

indicators.note: these letters are rearranged to form a new word, the answer made from them

explanation.surface: A toothed wheel that clatters noisily when it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel with angled teeth and a pawl allows motion in a single direction, clicking as it goes.
